"Mining Meaning: Measurement Error in AI-Assisted Literature Reviews"

The paper compared three approaches:
- Zero-shot: Give the model the paper and instructions, without labeled examples.
- RAG: Give it relevant examples from previously labeled papers.
- SFT (Supervised fine-tuning): Train the model further on human-labeled examples.

SFT generally performed best at the harder extraction tasks. RAG tended to report things that weren't there.

https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27686
